title: Anaerobic respiration

draft.title: Anaerobic respiration
card: Anaerobic respiration happens without oxygen. Glucose is broken down only by glycolysis in the cytosol, which makes a net 2 ATP per glucose.
pyruvate is changed to lactic acid. No carbon dioxide is made in this step, and the lactic acid can build up in muscle during hard exercise.
pyruvate is changed to ethanol and carbon dioxide. Yeast does this when it ferments sugar without oxygen.
Aerobic respiration makes about 30 to 32 ATP per glucose. The anaerobic pathways make far less, because the energy in the products is not released.
draft.remember: No oxygen means glycolysis only: 2 ATP, with lactic acid in animals or ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast.

a.q: A yeast culture in a sealed jar has run out of oxygen. Which products does it now make from glucose?
a.why: Yeast without oxygen changes pyruvate to ethanol and carbon dioxide. Lactic acid is the animal pathway, so it is the tempting wrong choice, and the animal pathway makes no carbon dioxide.
a.clue: Yeast and animals use different anaerobic products.

b.q: Sam sprints hard and his muscle cells run short of oxygen. Which statement correctly describes what happens in his muscle cells?
opts: Glucose gives a net 2 ATP and lactic acid forms
Glucose gives a net 2 ATP and ethanol forms
Glucose gives 30 ATP and lactic acid forms
Glucose gives 30 ATP and ethanol forms
b.why: Without enough oxygen, only glycolysis runs, so the net gain is 2 ATP per glucose. Animal cells make lactic acid, not ethanol. The figure of about 30 ATP needs oxygen, so it does not fit here.
b.clue: Check both the ATP amount and which organism the cells belong to.

b.best: Glucose gives a net 2 ATP and lactic acid forms
